issues.display_title: Issue #1423: Fix Issue Ghost File (Empty Thumbnail) Appears After Renaming
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Description

A state management bug occurs in the File Manager when a user renames a file.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Select a file in the File Manager.
  2. Rename the file (e.g. remove the word "copy" from the end of the filename).
  3. Issue: An empty thumbnail (a broken/crossed image box) appears next to the newly renamed file. The UI retains the old file object with a broken path reference while simultaneously rendering the updated file.
  4. Workaround: Reloading the application clears the ghost file.

Screenshot (user)

The user has 4 images; after renaming one (removing the trailing "copy" text), an empty pano / broken thumbnail is displayed next to it.

"I have 4 images here, I renamed one by removing the copy text from the end, and it displayed an empty pano…" "If I reload the empty image disappears" (Attach the annotated screenshot here — drag-and-drop into the issue to embed.)

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): the File Manager & Preview module renders the file/thumbnail grid (real-time via chokidar + thumbnail DB). This is a renderer state bug in that grid after a rename.
  • §7 (reliability & trust): ghost/broken thumbnails undermine confidence in the core daily-driver surface.

Root cause (suspected)

On a successful rename, the frontend state array isn't updated in place — instead a new file object is appended while the stale object (with the old/broken path) is left behind, producing a duplicate "ghost" entry with a broken thumbnail until reload.

Sub-tasks

  • Audit Rename Handler: Inspect the onRenameSuccess function. Ensure that when a successful response is received, the frontend state array is updated correctly.
  • Fix State Mutation: The logic should find the specific file's index in the state array and update its name/path property directly. It must NOT append a new object while leaving the stale object behind. Ensure the thumbnail/cache key follows the new path.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Renaming a file instantly updates the name on the existing thumbnail.
  2. No empty boxes or broken image thumbnails are spawned after a rename operation.
  3. The UI updates reactively without requiring a page reload.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: App build with the fix installed · a folder containing several 360°/image files, including filenames ending in "copy".

TC1 — Rename (remove "copy") — primary

  1. Select a file whose name ends with "copy" and rename it (remove the "copy" text).
  2. Expected: The existing thumbnail updates to the new name in place; no ghost/broken/empty thumbnail appears; no reload needed.

TC2 — General Rename

  1. Rename a file to an arbitrary new name (and rename one back).
  2. Expected: Single entry updates in place each time; no duplicate/ghost entries; thumbnail still renders correctly.

TC3 — No Reload Required (AC #3)

  1. After several renames, do not reload.
  2. Expected: Grid state is correct without reload; the previously-needed workaround (reload) is no longer necessary.

TC4 — Sort / Count Integrity

  1. With the grid sorted by Name/Date, rename a file and observe ordering and item count.
  2. Expected: Item count stays correct (no extra ghost item); sorting reflows correctly for the new name.

TC5 — Rename Collision / Cancel (resilience)

  1. Attempt a rename to an existing name (or cancel mid-rename).
  2. Expected: Handled gracefully — no ghost entry, no broken thumbnail, clear feedback; state remains consistent.

TC6 — Cross-Platform

  1. Repeat TC1 on Windows and macOS if available.
  2. Expected: No ghost thumbnail on either platform.

issues.display_title: Issue #1424: Fix Issue Visual Duplicates Appear After Move and Copy Operations
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Description

A state hydration bug occurs in the File Manager's split-panel view when moving and copying files, resulting in visual duplicates.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Move a batch of files from the left panel to the right panel.
  2. Copy those same files back from the right panel to the left panel.
  3. Issue: The files in the left panel are now displayed twice (duplicated) in the UI grid. The frontend state array appears to be appending the newly copied data without clearing the previous state or checking for existing UI elements.
  4. Workaround: Reloading the application removes the visual duplicates.

Screenshot (user)

Split-panel view: the user moved all panos to the right, then copied them back to the left — the left grid then shows each image twice.

  1. "I've moved all the panos to the right, by mistake, I usually copy them"
  2. "I copied the images back to left"
  3. "the images are displayed as duplicates"

(Attach the annotated screenshot here — drag-and-drop into the issue to embed.)

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): the File Manager & Preview module is the dual-panel grid with a real-time filesystem watcher (chokidar). This is a renderer state-hydration bug in that grid after move/copy.
  • §7 (reliability & trust): duplicated entries erode trust in the core file-management surface.
  • Related: #1423 — Ghost File (Empty Thumbnail) After Renaming — same class of "append instead of re-hydrate" state bug in the File Manager grid.

Root cause (suspected)

On move/copy success, the UI grid's state array is appended with the new file data instead of re-hydrating from the actual folder contents (or de-duping by file ID/path), leaving duplicate entries until a reload.

Sub-tasks

  • Audit Move/Copy Handlers: Inspect the onMoveSuccess and onCopySuccess state-update logic.
  • Fix Array Appending Logic: When files are copied or moved, the UI grid should cleanly re-hydrate the file list from the actual folder status, or check whether the file IDs/paths already exist in the UI before appending to the state array.
  • Implement File Watcher (optional): Consider using a filesystem watcher (chokidar already in the stack) to auto-trigger UI state refreshes when folder contents change, bypassing manual array manipulation.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Copying or moving files between panels accurately updates the file count and display.
  2. No visual duplicates are rendered in the grid after consecutive Move and Copy operations.
  3. The UI reflects the true state of the local file system instantly without requiring a page reload.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: App build with the fix installed · two folders open in the split panels · a batch of several image/360 files.

TC1 — Move then Copy Back (primary)

  1. Move a batch of files from the left panel to the right.
  2. Copy those same files back from the right panel to the left.
  3. Expected: Left grid shows each file once (no duplicates); count is correct; no reload needed.

TC2 — Copy Into Same Folder / Existing Files

  1. Copy files into a panel that already contains some of them.
  2. Expected: Grid reflects the true folder contents (no phantom duplicates); existing vs. new files handled per OS copy behavior; count accurate.

TC3 — Repeated / Consecutive Operations

  1. Perform several consecutive move/copy operations back and forth.
  2. Expected: No accumulation of duplicate entries across repeated operations; state stays consistent.

TC4 — Both Panels Reflect Truth

  1. After move/copy, compare each panel's grid to the actual folder contents in the OS file explorer.
  2. Expected: Both panels match the real filesystem state (count + names) without reload.

TC5 — No Reload Required (AC #3)

  1. Do not reload after the operations.
  2. Expected: Correct, de-duplicated state without the reload workaround.

TC6 — Cross-Platform

  1. Repeat TC1 on Windows and macOS if available.
  2. Expected: No duplicates on either platform.

issues.display_title: Issue #1418: Implement Flat Mode 360 Video Support in New Three.js Viewer
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Overview

Add a Flat projection mode for 360° video playback in the new Three.js / React Three Fiber viewer. This extends the base 360° video support (#1410) with a flat projection: render the equirectangular video frame on a flat 2D plane (rectilinear / unwrapped flat view) instead of mapping it onto the inside of a sphere.

Sibling of #1410 (standard 360° video) — same engine/pipeline, different projection. See also #1414 (Preview video menu UI).

DESIGN

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): the File Manager & Preview module hosts the Three.js / React Three Fiber 360° viewer; this adds a projection mode to that viewer.
  • §4 / §7: richer Preview projections deepen the Import → Preview → Publish path and must keep the "fast viewer" quality bar.

Sub-tasks

Sub-task 1 — Flat Projection Rendering

Extend the viewer so a 360° video source (mapped to a VideoTexture, per #1410) can be rendered in a flat projection — display the equirectangular frame on a flat plane (rectilinear/unwrapped), with live video playback on the texture.

Sub-task 2 — Projection Mode Switch (UI)

Add a control to switch the active video into Flat mode (alongside the standard 360 view), integrated with the Preview video menu (#1414). Switching modes must not interrupt playback position/state.

Sub-task 3 — Performance & Buffering

Maintain the fast performance of the new viewer during flat-mode video playback. Preserve loading/buffering states (spinner) and smooth pan/zoom interaction within the flat view.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A 360° video can be rendered in Flat projection in the new viewer, with live playback.
  • User can switch a playing video into/out of Flat mode without losing playback position; controls (play/pause, scrubber, volume, full-screen) still work.
  • Buffering/loading state is shown; no viewer performance regression vs. standard 360 video playback.
  • Standard 360° video (#1410) and still-image preview are unaffected (no regression).

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: Build installed (note GPU/CPU/RAM/OS) · a normal 360° equirectangular video, a high-res/high-bitrate video, and a still 360° image (regression) ready.

TC1 — Flat Render

  1. Open a 360° video, switch to Flat mode.
  2. Expected: The equirectangular frame renders flat (rectilinear/unwrapped) with live playback; pan/zoom works as designed for the mode.

TC2 — Mode Switch Without Interruption

  1. While the video is playing in standard 360 mode, switch to Flat (and back).
  2. Expected: Playback position and play/pause state are preserved across the switch; no flicker/crash.

TC3 — Controls in Flat

  1. In Flat mode use play/pause, scrubber, volume, full-screen.
  2. Expected: All controls function correctly.

TC4 — Performance & Buffering

  1. Play the high-res video in Flat mode and seek to an unbuffered position.
  2. Expected: Buffering indicator shows; playback resumes smoothly; no significant frame drops vs. standard 360 playback.

TC5 — Regression

  1. Open standard 360° video (#1410) and a still 360° image.
  2. Expected: Both behave as before — Flat mode does not regress them.

issues.display_title: Issue #1410: Implement 360 Video Support in New Three.js Viewer
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Overview

Extend the new Three.js / React Three Fiber 360° viewer to support 360° video playback, in addition to the existing 360° image preview.

DESIGN

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): the File Manager & Preview module provides the 360° interactive viewer built on Three.js / React Three Fiber. This task extends that viewer from still panoramas to video sources.
  • §4 (North Star / funnel): richer Preview capability deepens the Import → Preview → Publish path and the value users get before publishing.
  • §7 (Roadmap — reliability & trust): the viewer is core daily-driver surface; video support must preserve the "fast viewer" quality bar.

Sub-tasks

Sub-task 1 — Three.js Video Integration

Modify the current Three.js viewer component to detect if the source is a video file. If it is, map the video source to a VideoTexture and render it onto the inner sphere/geometry.

Sub-task 2 — Video Player UI Controls

Develop and overlay standard video controls on top of the 360 canvas. This must include:

  • Play / Pause button
  • Timeline / scrubber for seeking
  • Volume control
  • Full-screen toggle

Sub-task 3 — Performance & Buffering

Implement loading / buffering states (e.g. a loading spinner) so the user knows when the video is fetching data. Ensure the fast performance of the new viewer is maintained during video playback.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A 360° video source is detected and rendered onto the sphere via VideoTexture in the new viewer.
  • Play/Pause, timeline scrubber, volume, and full-screen controls work over the 360 canvas.
  • Buffering/loading state is shown while the video fetches; playback stays smooth with no viewer performance regression.
  • Existing 360° image preview is unaffected (no regression).

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: App build with the fix installed · at least one tester machine (note GPU/CPU/RAM and OS) · sample media ready (see below). Record source resolution, duration, and codec/container of each video.

Test data to prepare:

  • A normal 360° equirectangular video (e.g. MP4/H.264, 2:1 ratio, with audio) — the main "happy path".
  • A high-resolution / high-bitrate 360° video (e.g. ≥ 4K) — for the performance/buffering check.
  • A 360° video without an audio track — to verify volume control behavior.
  • A regular 360° image (still panorama) — regression check (must still preview as before).
  • A non-360 / non-video file (e.g. a normal photo, a corrupt/unsupported video) — negative check.

TC1 — Video Detection & Render (Sub-task 1)

  1. Open the normal 360° video in the new Three.js viewer.
  2. Expected: The source is detected as video, mapped to a VideoTexture, and rendered onto the inner sphere; the panorama is navigable (drag to look around) while the video plays.

TC2 — Player Controls (Sub-task 2)

  1. With the video open, use each control: Play/Pause, timeline scrubber (seek forward/back), volume (mute/adjust), full-screen toggle.
  2. Expected: Play/Pause toggles playback; scrubber seeks accurately and the frame updates; volume changes audio level / mutes; full-screen enters and exits cleanly with controls still usable.

TC3 — Buffering & Loading State (Sub-task 3)

  1. Open the high-res / high-bitrate video (throttle the network/disk if the source is remote) and seek to an unbuffered position.
  2. Expected: A loading/buffering indicator (e.g. spinner) appears while data is fetched, then playback resumes; no frozen frame without feedback.

TC4 — Playback Performance (Sub-task 3)

  1. Play the high-res video and simultaneously rotate/zoom the 360 view.
  2. Expected: Playback stays smooth; rotation/zoom remain responsive; no significant frame drops or stutter vs. image preview — the "fast viewer" quality bar is maintained.

TC5 — Audio Edge Case

  1. Open the 360° video that has no audio track and operate the volume control.
  2. Expected: No crash or error; volume control degrades gracefully (disabled or no-op); video still plays.

TC6 — Image Preview Regression

  1. Open a regular 360° still image in the same viewer.
  2. Expected: Image preview behaves exactly as before — no video controls shown, no errors, no performance regression.

TC7 — Negative / Unsupported Input

  1. Try opening a non-360 image and a corrupt/unsupported video file.
  2. Expected: Clear handling — image opens as a normal preview (no video controls); unsupported/corrupt video shows a friendly error, not a raw stack trace or crash.

Reference

docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md §3 (Preview module), §4 (funnel), §7 (roadmap).

issues.display_title: Issue #1411: Auto Level Engine Fails due to OpenCV Code Signature & Missing dylib Error on Mac Version
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

A critical application error occurs on macOS when triggering the leveling engine (Auto Level). Instead of processing the image, the application throws a fatal system error regarding dynamic library loading (.dylib).

The error log specifically highlights:

  1. Code Signature Mismatch: mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs. macOS Gatekeeper is blocking the OpenCV library (libopencv_imgcodecs.413.dylib) from executing because it is not signed with the same Apple Developer certificate as the main GoThru application.
  2. Hardcoded Homebrew Paths: The engine is trying to look for the library at local Homebrew paths (e.g. /opt/homebrew/opt/opencv/lib/...). This means the dependency is not properly bundled within the application package and will crash on any user's Mac that doesn't have OpenCV installed via Homebrew.

Impact

Auto Level is fully broken on macOS for any user without a matching Homebrew OpenCV install — i.e. effectively all normal end users. This is a release blocker for the Mac build.

Context / Reference

This is the "Native-binary fragility" risk flagged in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md §8 — "several modules shell out to bundled binaries; failures surface as raw stderr and are OS/arch-sensitive." Auto Level is part of the core Edit suite (§3) and the reliability & trust theme (§7). The same bundling/signing fix likely benefits other binary-backed Mac modules (Enfuse, conversions, nadir, AI staging).

Root-cause directions

  • The OpenCV dylib (libopencv_imgcodecs.413.dylib) must be bundled inside the app package and the engine binary's load paths rewritten from absolute Homebrew paths to @rpath / @executable_path (e.g. via install_name_tool / otool -L verification).
  • The bundled dylib must be code-signed with the same Team ID as the main app and included in notarization, so Gatekeeper allows it.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Auto Level runs successfully on a clean macOS machine that has never installed OpenCV via Homebrew.
  • otool -L on the engine binary shows no /opt/homebrew/... (or other absolute local) paths — only bundled/@rpath references.
  • The bundled libopencv_*.dylib is signed with the same Team ID as the app and passes notarization; no "different Team IDs" Gatekeeper error.
  • Works on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
  • No regression to Auto Level on Windows.

Test Source Image

Use this sample for the leveling test: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1P1tVuo1vXFg1Yl6objPcjNwxbKD-aUH-/view?usp=sharing

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions:

  • A signed + notarized macOS build of the app, installed the way a real user would (downloaded → quarantine attribute present), not run from a dev tree.
  • At least one clean Mac that has never installed Homebrew OpenCV (critical — this is the failure condition). Ideally one Apple Silicon and one Intel machine. Note OS version + chip.
  • The test source image above downloaded locally.

TC1 — Auto Level on a Clean Mac (primary)

  1. On the clean Mac (no Homebrew OpenCV), open Edit → Auto Level and add the test source image.
  2. Apply / run Auto Level.
  3. Expected: The image is leveled and saved successfully. No .dylib / "different Team IDs" error; no crash.

TC2 — No Hardcoded Homebrew Paths

  1. In Terminal, run otool -L on the Auto Level engine binary (and otool -L on the bundled libopencv_imgcodecs.*.dylib).
  2. Expected: Dependency paths point to bundled/@rpath/@executable_path locations — no /opt/homebrew/... or other absolute local paths.

TC3 — Code Signature / Team ID Consistency

  1. Run codesign -dv --verbose=4 on the app and on the bundled OpenCV dylib(s).
  2. Expected: The dylib(s) are signed with the same Team ID / Authority as the main app and are covered by notarization. spctl -a -vvv on the app passes.
  3. Confirm the system log shows no mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs entry during Auto Level.

TC4 — Apple Silicon & Intel Coverage

  1. Repeat TC1 on both an Apple Silicon and an Intel Mac (and the correct universal/arch build).
  2. Expected: Auto Level succeeds on both architectures.

TC5 — Gatekeeper / First-Run Quarantine

  1. Install the build fresh from the distributed artifact (so the quarantine flag is set) on the clean Mac and run Auto Level on first launch.
  2. Expected: No Gatekeeper block on the OpenCV library; Auto Level works on first run without the user manually allowing libraries.

TC6 — Output Integrity (regression)

  1. Inspect the TC1 output.
  2. Expected: Valid, viewable, correctly-leveled 360° image; metadata (GPS, GPano/XMP) preserved — consistent with normal Auto Level behavior.

TC7 — Windows Regression

  1. Run Auto Level with the same source image on Windows.
  2. Expected: Still works as before — no regression introduced by the Mac bundling/signing fix.

issues.display_title: Issue #1415: Implement Collapsible in Quick Access File Manager
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Overview

Implement the collapsible Quick Access / File Manager sidebar in the app (renderer / React + Redux). This is the engineering implementation of the UI design task #1412 (project: UI Design) — by default the sidebar loads in a "folded" (minimized) state to optimize the workspace area.

Design Reference

  • UI design task: #1412 — Create Collapsible File Manager Sidebar (sub-tasks + acceptance criteria).
  • Figma design: https://www.figma.com/design/zanXCkiJELjiRNx4RayJ6N/NEW-GoThru-Photo-Studio-_-360-Image-Viewer-Desktop-App?node-id=25511-726785&t=w39Rlfb3kAPv9ePb-0

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): the File Manager module is the workspace entry point (dual-panel, resizable). Collapsing Quick Access reclaims canvas space for the viewer/edit area.
  • §7 (roadmap / UX polish): a cleaner, denser workspace supports the core daily-driver flow.

Sub-tasks (implementation)

  • Toggle Button: Add a fold/expand icon button (chevron or hamburger) at the top or bottom of the Quick Access sidebar, wired to a collapse/expand handler.
  • Default State (collapsed): Set the initial render state of the sidebar to collapsed/minimized on app load, per the Figma.
  • State persistence: Persist the expanded/collapsed preference (Redux + settings/NeDB or local storage) so it survives reloads — or default to collapsed if no stored preference.
  • Collapsed UI: When folded, hide all folder text labels and reduce folder icon size to the mini variant shown in Figma; expanded restores full labels.
  • Hover tooltips: When collapsed, hovering a mini folder icon shows a tooltip with the folder's name (use existing HeroUI tooltip; keyboard-accessible).
  • Smooth transition: Animate the width/expand-collapse transition smoothly (Framer Motion / CSS), matching the design; no layout jump in the adjacent panels.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. User can smoothly toggle the sidebar between expanded and collapsed states.
  2. The app remembers, or defaults to, the collapsed state upon initial load.
  3. Folder names are easily discoverable via hover tooltips when in the collapsed state.
  4. Implementation matches the Figma design (mini icons, spacing, toggle placement) and the existing design system (HeroUI/Tailwind, light & dark themes).
  5. No regression to dual-panel resize, folder navigation, or selection.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: App build with the change installed · a folder tree with several Quick Access entries (varying name lengths) · test on both light and dark themes; Windows and macOS if available.

TC1 — Default Collapsed State (AC #2)

  1. Launch the app fresh (first run / no stored preference).
  2. Expected: The Quick Access / File Manager sidebar loads in the collapsed (mini) state — folder labels hidden, mini icons shown — matching the Figma.

TC2 — Toggle Expand/Collapse (AC #1)

  1. Click the fold/expand toggle button.
  2. Expected: Sidebar smoothly expands to show full folder labels; clicking again smoothly collapses it. Animation is fluid with no flicker or layout jump in adjacent panels.

TC3 — Hover Tooltips When Collapsed (AC #3)

  1. With the sidebar collapsed, hover over each mini folder icon.
  2. Expected: A tooltip shows the correct folder name (incl. long names); tooltip appears/dismisses cleanly and is reachable via keyboard focus.

TC4 — State Persistence

  1. Toggle to expanded, then close and reopen the app. Then toggle to collapsed and reopen again.
  2. Expected: The sidebar restores the last chosen state on reload (or defaults to collapsed if persistence is by-design defaulted) — behavior consistent with AC #2.

TC5 — Functional Parity in Both States

  1. In both collapsed and expanded states, click folders to navigate and select items.
  2. Expected: Navigation and selection work identically in both states; collapsing does not break click targets or routing.

TC6 — Visual / Theme Consistency

  1. Inspect the sidebar in light and dark themes (and at different window/panel sizes).
  2. Expected: Matches Figma; icons, spacing, and the toggle render correctly; consistent with HeroUI/Tailwind styling; no clipping or overflow.

TC7 — Regression

  1. Resize the dual panels; use other File Manager controls.
  2. Expected: Panel resize and existing File Manager features behave as before — no regression introduced by the collapsible sidebar.

Related

  • UI design: #1412 — Create Collapsible File Manager Sidebar.

issues.display_title: Issue #1419: Detect EXIF for 360 Video File in Preview
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Overview

Detect and read metadata (EXIF / video container + spherical/XMP tags) for 360° video files so the app can recognize a video as a 360° panorama and surface its info in Preview — the same way it already does for 360° still images.

This is the detection/metadata layer that the new video viewer work depends on: the viewer needs to know a file is a (360°) video, its dimensions/duration/codec, and whether it carries spherical-video metadata, in order to choose the correct projection and render it.

Related tasks

This task is related to (and a prerequisite/companion of):

  • #1410 — Implement 360 Video Support in New Three.js Viewer
  • #1417 — Implement Fish Eye Mode 360 Video Support in New Three.js Viewer
  • #1418 — Implement Flat Mode 360 Video Support in New Three.js Viewer

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): the File Manager & Preview module already reads image metadata via exifr / exiftool-vendored (GPS, GPano/XMP). This extends that detection to video files.
  • §4 (funnel): correct detection at Import → Preview is what lets a video enter the viewer pipeline at all.
  • §8 (metadata integrity): GPS / spherical (GPano-style) metadata must be read reliably so 360° videos are recognized and positioned correctly.

Scope / What "EXIF for video" means

Video files (e.g. MP4/MOV) don't carry classic JPEG EXIF; the equivalent metadata lives in the container/track metadata and Spherical Video (V1/V2) / XMP-GPano tags. Detection should cover:

  • File type detection (is this a video; is it a supported container/codec).
  • Technical metadata: dimensions (width/height, 2:1 check), duration, frame rate, codec, bitrate.
  • Spherical/360 metadata: Spherical Video tags (e.g. Spherical, ProjectionType = equirectangular), GPano/XMP equivalents, stereo mode if present.
  • Geo/other: GPS coordinates if embedded, creation date, camera/make-model where available.

Sub-tasks

  • Video type detection: Detect video files in File Manager / Preview and distinguish them from images (extension + container sniffing).
  • Metadata extraction: Read video container + spherical/XMP metadata (extend the existing exiftool-vendored path; exiftool reads MP4/MOV + Spherical/GPano tags) — dimensions, duration, codec, projection type, GPS.
  • 360 recognition flag: Derive an is360/projectionType signal the viewer (#1410/#1417/#1418) can consume to pick the right projection (equirect / fisheye / flat).
  • Surface in Preview UI: Show the detected video metadata (resolution, duration, codec, 360 yes/no, GPS) in the existing Preview/file-info panel.
  • Graceful handling: Non-360 videos, missing/partial metadata, and unsupported codecs are handled without crashing and reported clearly.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The app detects a video file in Preview/File Manager and reads its metadata (dimensions, duration, codec, projection/spherical tags, GPS when present).
  2. A 360° (equirectangular/spherical) video is correctly recognized via its metadata and exposes a signal the viewer (#1410/#1417/#1418) can use to choose the projection.
  3. Detected metadata is shown in the Preview/file-info UI, consistent with how image metadata is displayed.
  4. Non-360 videos and files with missing/partial metadata are handled gracefully (no crash, clear state).

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: Build installed · sample media ready (record each file's known specs beforehand).

Test data to prepare:

  • A true 360° equirectangular video with Spherical/GPano metadata (2:1, MP4/MOV).
  • A non-360 regular video (e.g. 16:9, no spherical tags).
  • A 360° video with GPS embedded.
  • A video with missing/stripped metadata and an unsupported/corrupt video — negative checks.
  • A 360° still image — regression (image metadata still reads as before).

TC1 — 360° Video Detected (primary)

  1. Select the 360° equirectangular video in File Manager / open Preview.
  2. Expected: Recognized as a video and as 360° / equirectangular; resolution, duration, codec read correctly; the viewer receives the projection signal.

TC2 — Metadata Shown in Preview

  1. Open the file-info / metadata panel for the video.
  2. Expected: Dimensions, duration, codec, projection type, and GPS (if present) are displayed consistently with image metadata.

TC3 — Non-360 Video

  1. Open the regular 16:9 video.
  2. Expected: Detected as a video but not 360; UI reflects that; no false 360 flag.

TC4 — GPS Extraction

  1. Open the 360° video with embedded GPS.
  2. Expected: GPS coordinates are read and available (e.g. for the map), matching the source.

TC5 — Missing / Corrupt Metadata

  1. Open the stripped-metadata video and the corrupt/unsupported video.
  2. Expected: Graceful handling — partial metadata shown where available; unsupported/corrupt shows a clear message; no crash or infinite spinner.

TC6 — Image Regression

  1. Open a 360° still image.
  2. Expected: Image EXIF/GPano detection still works exactly as before — no regression from the video changes.

issues.display_title: Issue #1425: Fix Special Character for Rename Feature
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Overview

Fix special-character handling in the Rename feature so files/folders can be renamed safely and consistently across the app. Renames containing special characters should be validated, sanitized, or properly escaped — and behave the same way everywhere the rename action is available.

Scope (sub-tasks — per module)

Apply the fix in each surface that exposes Rename:

  • Preview — renaming from the Preview context.
  • Edit — renaming from the Edit module / output naming.
  • File Manager — renaming files/folders in the dual-panel grid.

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): rename is shared across the File Manager, Preview, and Edit surfaces; behavior should be consistent across all three.
  • §8 (metadata/OS sensitivity): filename rules differ per OS (Windows vs macOS reserved characters), so special-character handling must be cross-platform.
  • Related: #1423 (rename ghost thumbnail) — same Rename feature; keep state-update behavior consistent when fixing this.

Problem / what "special character" covers

Renames involving characters such as:

  • OS-reserved/invalid filename characters (e.g. Windows: \ / : * ? " < > |; control chars; trailing dot/space).
  • Unicode / non-ASCII / emoji / accented characters.
  • Leading/trailing whitespace, very long names, and reserved device names (e.g. CON, NUL on Windows).

These should not crash, silently fail, corrupt the path, or produce inconsistent results between modules.

Sub-tasks (implementation detail)

  • Shared validation/sanitization: Centralize a rename validation/sanitize helper (allow vs. block vs. escape) and use it across Preview, Edit, and File Manager so all three behave identically.
  • Cross-platform rules: Enforce Windows + macOS filename constraints; handle reserved names and trailing dot/space.
  • Clear feedback: When a name is invalid, show a friendly inline message instead of failing silently or throwing.
  • Correct write + state update: Ensure the actual file rename and the UI state reflect the sanitized/accepted name consistently (no ghost/duplicate entries — see #1423).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Renaming with special characters works (or is rejected with a clear message) consistently in Preview, Edit, and File Manager.
  2. No crash, silent failure, or corrupted/broken path when special characters are used.
  3. Cross-platform filename rules are respected (Windows & macOS); reserved/invalid characters handled gracefully.
  4. The UI updates correctly to the final accepted name with no ghost/duplicate entries.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: Build installed · test on Windows and macOS if available · sample files/folders ready.

TC1 — Special Characters in File Manager

  1. In File Manager, rename a file using special characters (e.g. name & (v2)!, accented café, emoji, then an invalid set like a/b:c?).
  2. Expected: Valid names apply correctly; invalid characters are blocked/sanitized with a clear message; no crash or broken thumbnail.

TC2 — Rename from Preview

  1. Rename a file from the Preview surface using the same character sets.
  2. Expected: Same behavior/validation as File Manager; name updates consistently.

TC3 — Rename from Edit

  1. Rename / set output filename from the Edit module using special characters.
  2. Expected: Same validation; output lands with the correct, sanitized name.

TC4 — Cross-Module Consistency

  1. Apply the same special-character rename in all three surfaces.
  2. Expected: Identical validation rules and results across Preview, Edit, and File Manager.

TC5 — OS Edge Cases

  1. Try reserved names (CON, NUL), trailing dot/space, and very long names.
  2. Expected: Handled gracefully per OS rules; clear messaging; no corruption.

TC6 — State Integrity (regression vs #1423)

  1. After a special-character rename, verify the grid.
  2. Expected: Single, correctly-named entry updated in place; no ghost/duplicate; no reload required.

Demo by developer

Overview

Implement a "Failed Auto-Update" message modal that clearly informs the user when the in-app auto-update fails, instead of failing silently or showing a raw error — and offers a recovery action (e.g. retry / download manual version).

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3: the app uses an auto-updater (appUpdater). When it fails, users currently get no clear, friendly feedback.
  • §7 (reliability & trust) / §8 (OS-sensitive native behavior): auto-update can fail for permissions/network/signing reasons; a friendly modal + recovery path preserves trust.
  • Related: "Implement Download Manual Version" (#1426) — the modal's primary recovery action.

Scope / Sub-tasks

  • Detect auto-update failure: Hook the updater's error/failed events.
  • Friendly modal: Show a clear, human-readable message (what happened + what to do) — not a raw stack trace.
  • Recovery actions: Offer Retry and Download manual version (links to #1426), plus Dismiss.
  • Localized + themed: Use i18n strings (19 locales) and match the existing modal design (HeroUI/Tailwind, light & dark).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When auto-update fails, a friendly modal appears with a clear message (no raw error/stack trace).
  2. The modal offers actionable recovery (Retry and/or Download manual version) and a dismiss option.
  3. The app remains usable after dismissing; no crash.
  4. Message is localized and consistent with the app's design system.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: A way to force an auto-update failure (block the update server / corrupt update / no network / insufficient permissions). Note OS.

TC1 — Failure Shows Modal (primary)

  1. Trigger an auto-update under a failure condition.
  2. Expected: A friendly "Failed Auto-Update" modal appears with a clear message — not a raw error/JSON/stack trace.

TC2 — Recovery Actions

  1. In the modal, use Retry and Download manual version.
  2. Expected: Retry re-attempts the update; Download routes to the manual-download flow (#1426); Dismiss closes the modal.

TC3 — App Stays Usable

  1. Dismiss the modal.
  2. Expected: App continues working normally; no crash or blocked UI.

TC4 — Localization & Theme

  1. Switch language and light/dark theme; re-trigger the failure.
  2. Expected: Modal text is localized; styling matches the design system in both themes.

TC5 — Success Path Unaffected (regression)

  1. Run a normal, successful auto-update.
  2. Expected: No failure modal shown; update completes as before.

Demo by developer

Overview

Implement a Download Manual Version capability so users can manually download/install a specific app version (e.g. when auto-update fails or they need a particular build) instead of relying solely on the in-app auto-updater.

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §1 / §3: the app ships an auto-updater (appUpdater) and shows an "Update Available" affordance. A manual-download path is the fallback when auto-update can't complete.
  • Related: the "Failed Auto-Update" message modal task (sibling) — the manual download is the recommended recovery action from that modal.

Scope / Sub-tasks

  • Manual download entry point: Add a clear UI action (e.g. in About / Update / the failed-update modal) to download the latest (or a manual) version.
  • Resolve & fetch the installer: Point to the correct release artifact for the user's OS/arch (Windows / macOS).
  • Progress + completion: Show download progress and a clear "installer ready" state; handle network errors gracefully.
  • Cross-platform: Correct artifact and behavior on Windows and macOS.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. User can trigger a manual download of the app version from a clear entry point.
  2. The correct OS/arch installer is fetched; progress and completion are shown.
  3. Network/download failures are handled with a friendly message and retry.
  4. Works on Windows and macOS.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: Build installed (note version + OS/arch) · network available; a way to simulate a network failure if possible.

TC1 — Manual Download (primary)

  1. Open the manual-download entry point and start the download.
  2. Expected: The correct installer for the current OS/arch downloads; progress is shown; on completion the installer/opening step is offered.

TC2 — Install the Downloaded Version

  1. Run the downloaded installer.
  2. Expected: App installs/updates to the expected version; launches normally afterward.

TC3 — Network Failure

  1. Trigger the download with no/interrupted network.
  2. Expected: Friendly error message; no crash; retry works once connectivity returns.

TC4 — Cross-Platform

  1. Repeat TC1 on Windows and macOS.
  2. Expected: Correct artifact and behavior on each.

TC5 — Entry From Failed-Update Modal

  1. From the "Failed Auto-Update" modal (sibling task), choose the manual download action.
  2. Expected: Routes to the manual download flow and completes.

issues.display_title: Issue #1428: "Unable to Load Files" Error When Renaming an Image Back to Its Original Name
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Description

An "Unable to Load Files" error appears when a user renames an image back to its original name.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. In the File Manager, rename an image (e.g. photo.jpg -> photo-1.jpg).
  2. Rename it back to its original name (photo-1.jpg -> photo.jpg).
  3. Issue: An "Unable to Load Files" error is shown (files fail to load / grid errors).

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): the File Manager grid loads files and thumbnails (thumbnail/dimension cache + chokidar watcher). Renaming back to a prior name likely collides with stale cache/state keyed by that name/path.
  • Related: #1423 (rename ghost thumbnail) and #1425 (special characters in rename) — same Rename feature; likely shared state/cache root cause.

Suspected root cause

Renaming back to the original name collides with a stale cache or state entry still keyed to that filename/path (thumbnail cache, dimension DB, or file-list state), causing the loader to error instead of resolving the file.

Sub-tasks

  • Audit rename -> reload path: Trace rename-back behavior: file-list refresh, thumbnail/dimension cache keys, and any path/ID reuse.
  • Fix stale-state collision: Ensure renaming back to a prior name cleanly re-resolves the file (invalidate/refresh stale cache/state for that path) without erroring.
  • Graceful load handling: If a load does fail, recover gracefully (re-hydrate from folder) rather than surfacing "Unable to Load Files".

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Renaming an image back to its original name loads the file correctly — no "Unable to Load Files" error.
  2. The grid and thumbnail render correctly after the rename-back, without a reload.
  3. No stale/ghost/duplicate entries result (consistent with #1423).

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: Build installed · a folder with several images · test on Windows and macOS if available.

TC1 — Rename Back to Original (primary)

  1. Rename photo.jpg -> photo-1.jpg, then rename it back to photo.jpg.
  2. Expected: File loads correctly; no "Unable to Load Files" error; thumbnail renders; no reload needed.

TC2 — Multiple Round-Trips

  1. Rename back and forth several times (original <-> temp name).
  2. Expected: Loads correctly every time; no accumulating errors or stale entries.

TC3 — Across Folders / Refresh

  1. Rename back, navigate away and back to the folder.
  2. Expected: Grid shows the correct file; no error; counts/thumbnails correct.

TC4 — Cache Integrity

  1. After rename-back, open the image in Preview.
  2. Expected: Correct (not stale) image/thumbnail loads; metadata intact.

TC5 — Cross-Platform

  1. Repeat TC1 on Windows and macOS.
  2. Expected: No "Unable to Load Files" error on either platform.

TC6 — Regression (related)

  1. Do a normal rename (not back to original) and a special-character rename.
  2. Expected: Still works (ties to #1423 / #1425); no ghost/duplicate or load error.

issues.display_title: Issue #1429: Fix Issue Auto Level Fails on Mac
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Auto Level fails on macOS. Running Auto Level on a batch results in every file failing — the queue shows Total: 23 Selected | 0 Queue | 0 Success | 23 Failed | 0 Canceled, with Roll/Pitch 0.0 and Status: Failed for each item. The error text on the rows references a "library not loaded" failure (dynamic library load error), and the batch reports "All process completed" with all items failed.

Team note (from chat): "please make sure you test and deliver a product that works before we actually move on to build something new."

Test Files

Sample files that reproduce the failure: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14r7eGYrvp2PYxwoemxjDPeYtmeAveG52?usp=sharing

Screenshot (user)

GoThru Photo Studio (macOS) — Auto Level queue with 23 / 23 Failed, each row showing a library-load error under the filename; toast: "All process completed".

albug: "auto Level fails on mac" (Attach the annotated screenshot here — drag-and-drop into the issue to embed.)

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): Auto Level is part of the core Edit suite, which shells out to bundled native binaries.
  • §8 (Native-binary fragility): the doc flags that bundled-binary modules surface raw errors and are OS/arch-sensitive — this Mac-wide failure is exactly that risk.
  • Related / likely duplicate root cause: #1411 — Auto Level Engine Fails due to OpenCV Code Signature & Missing dylib Error on Mac (libopencv_imgcodecs.*.dylib not signed with the app's Team ID / hardcoded Homebrew paths). The "library not loaded" failure here is almost certainly the same bundling/signing problem.

Suspected root cause

The Auto Level engine's native dependency (OpenCV .dylib) is not bundled/signed correctly in the Mac build, so the dynamic loader can't load it on a normal user machine → every file fails. See #1411 for the dylib/Team-ID/@rpath details.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Auto Level processes the sample test files successfully on macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) — no "library not loaded" failures.
  2. The bundled native library loads on a clean Mac that has never installed dependencies via Homebrew.
  3. A batch reports real per-file success; failures (if any) show a friendly, specific message — not a raw library-load dump.
  4. No regression to Auto Level on Windows.

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions:

  • A signed + notarized macOS build, installed like a real user (downloaded, quarantine set) — not from a dev tree.
  • A clean Mac with no Homebrew-installed OpenCV (critical). Ideally one Apple Silicon and one Intel machine; note macOS version + chip.
  • Download the test files from the Drive link above.

TC1 — Auto Level Batch on Mac (primary)

  1. Add the downloaded sample files to the Auto Level queue and run.
  2. Expected: Files process to Success (with real Roll/Pitch values); no "library not loaded" / dylib errors; output saved.

TC2 — Single File

  1. Run Auto Level on one sample file.
  2. Expected: Succeeds; leveled output produced; metadata preserved.

TC3 — Clean Mac (no Homebrew)

  1. Run TC1 on a Mac that has never installed OpenCV via Homebrew.
  2. Expected: Still succeeds — the native library is bundled with the app (ties to #1411).

TC4 — Apple Silicon & Intel

  1. Repeat TC1 on both architectures (correct universal/arch build).
  2. Expected: Succeeds on both.

TC5 — Failure Messaging

  1. If any file genuinely fails (e.g. correction too large / unsupported), observe the row error.
  2. Expected: A friendly, specific message — not a raw "library not loaded" / stack dump; other items keep processing.

TC6 — Output Integrity

  1. Inspect successful outputs.
  2. Expected: Valid, correctly-leveled 360° images; GPS/GPano/XMP metadata preserved.

TC7 — Windows Regression

  1. Run Auto Level with the same files on Windows.
  2. Expected: Works as before — no regression from the Mac fix.

issues.display_title: Issue #1430: Fix Duplicate .pts Files in File Manager After Rename
issues.main_description_html:
Description

After renaming a file in the File Manager, duplicate .pts files appear in the grid. The .pts sidecar (panorama point/control file associated with an image) is not handled cleanly on rename — the UI (and/or the filesystem) ends up showing the .pts entry twice.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. In the File Manager, open a folder containing images with associated .pts sidecar files (e.g. KAN_1582-HDR Panorama.pts).
  2. Rename the related file.
  3. Issue: A duplicate .pts file appears in the grid (the old .pts entry remains alongside a new one).

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): the File Manager grid renders files (incl. .pts sidecars) with a real-time chokidar watcher + thumbnail/dimension cache. Rename should update sidecar entries in place, not duplicate them.
  • Related (same Rename / state-hydration family): #1423 (ghost thumbnail after rename), #1424 (duplicates after move/copy), #1428 ("Unable to Load Files" on rename-back), #1425 (special characters in rename). Likely the same "append instead of re-hydrate / stale-key" root cause.

Suspected root cause

On rename, the file-list state is appended with the new entry (and/or the .pts sidecar is re-added) without removing the stale .pts object — or the grid isn't re-hydrated from the actual folder contents — producing a duplicate .pts until reload.

Sub-tasks

  • Audit rename + sidecar handling: Inspect how .pts sidecars are tracked/updated in the rename handler and the file-list state.
  • Fix duplicate state: On rename, update the existing entry (and its .pts) in place, or re-hydrate the list from the folder / de-dupe by path — do not append a stale duplicate.
  • Confirm filesystem vs UI: Verify whether the duplicate is only visual (state) or an actual filesystem duplicate, and handle accordingly.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Renaming a file does not create duplicate .pts entries in the File Manager grid.
  2. The grid reflects the true folder contents (correct count, single .pts per file) without a reload.
  3. No regression to normal rename, move/copy, or thumbnail rendering (consistent with #1423 / #1424 / #1428).

Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Pre-conditions: Build installed · a folder containing images with .pts sidecar files · test on Windows and macOS if available.

TC1 — Rename With .pts Sidecar (primary)

  1. Rename a file that has an associated .pts sidecar.
  2. Expected: The .pts entry updates in place; no duplicate .pts appears; count is correct; no reload needed.

TC2 — Verify Filesystem

  1. After TC1, check the folder in the OS file explorer.
  2. Expected: Exactly one .pts per file on disk (no actual duplicate); UI matches the filesystem.

TC3 — Multiple / Repeated Renames

  1. Rename several files (and rename one back) in a folder with .pts files.
  2. Expected: No accumulation of duplicate .pts entries across operations.

TC4 — Sort / Count Integrity

  1. With the grid sorted by Name, rename a file and observe the .pts ordering and total count.
  2. Expected: Count correct; no phantom duplicate; sort reflows correctly.

TC5 — No Reload Required

  1. Do not reload after renaming.
  2. Expected: Grid is correct without the reload workaround.

TC6 — Cross-Platform

  1. Repeat TC1 on Windows and macOS.
  2. Expected: No duplicate .pts on either platform.
